items.title: P&H High Court initiates contempt case against The Hindu, Dainik Bhaskar over Dera Sacha Sauda propaganda ads
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has initiated suo motu contempt of court proceedings against the editors-in-chief and publishers of The Hindu and Dainik Bhaskar for publishing Dera Sacha Sauda advertisements claiming that its chief, Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh, was being targeted as part of a conspiracy. The matter was today listed before a bench of Justice Vinod S Bhardwaj and Justice Ravinder Malik . The Court listed it for consideration on November 25. Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh is currently serving a 20-year sentence for raping his two disciples. His appeal challenging the conviction and sentence is pending before the High Court. The High Court in 2024 and in March this year had acquitted him in two different murders cases. On September 12, the newspapers published a front-page advertisement which claimed that there was a conspiracy against Ram Rahim. The Hindu later issued a public apology for publishing the advertisement following public backlash. The issue has now got revived in view of the suo motu contempt proceedings initiated on an order passed by Justice Subhas Mehla who said the newspaper advertisements insinuated that courts were a party to the alleged conspiracy. The judge said that the advertisements were an attempt to mobilize public opinion and influence the judicial process, adding that such action directly obstructs the administration of justice. "On a prima facie consideration of the aforesaid advertisement publications, this Court is of the view that the contents thereof may have the tendency to scandalise or lower the authority of this Court," the judge added. Thus, he opined that the matter warrants examination of the publications in contempt jurisdiction. "Accordingly, this Court takes suo motu cognizance of criminal contempt under Article 215 of the Constitution of India read with Section 2(c)(i), 2(c)(iii) and 15(1) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971," Justice Mehla said in the reference order passed last month. items.title: CJI Surya Kant to attend NLSIU convocation on October 17
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant will attend the 34th annual convocation of the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru on October 17. The convocation will be held from 11 am to 1 pm at the Jnana Jyoti Auditorium on Palace Road, Bengaluru. Justice Kant, who is the Chancellor of NLSIU, will preside over the ceremony, the University said in an invitation circulated to invitees. The convocation comes after NLSIU had earlier cancelled the ceremony scheduled for September 12 after issuing a notice announcing that no convocation would be held for the 2026 batch due to "unavoidable circumstances" and that students would be conferred their degrees in absentia. The cancellation came amid a controversy over the proposed presence of CJI Kant and Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra at the ceremony. More than 700 current students, graduating students and alumni had objected to their participation. The development followed a separate controversy at NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad, where students had opposed the proposed presence of CJI Kant at their convocation. The issue escalated on August 13 when the BCI directed State Bar Councils to halt the enrolment of NALSAR's graduating batch, after which the direction was withdrawn within hours . NLSIU students and alumni subsequently expressed solidarity with the NALSAR students and criticised the BCI's action. On August 15, over 700 members of the NLSIU community signed a statement objecting to BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra and CJI Surya Kant attending NLSIU's convocation. According to reports, CJI Kant subsequently met NLSIU students to hear their concerns. Students were later asked to vote on whether they would attend a convocation at which the CJI would be present. A majority supported the arrangement, with the understanding that Mishra would not attend. However, the issue resurfaced after students were subsequently asked to publicly invite the CJI to the ceremony. The graduating batch did not agree to the additional demand, following which the September 12 convocation was cancelled. NLSIU's governing bodies later approved October 17 as the new date for the convocation. Students were given the option of receiving their degrees in person at the ceremony or in absentia. items.title: NCLT orders winding up of 14 Popular Finance-linked entities; asks liquidator to trace money, recover assets
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) at Kochi has ordered the winding up of 14 entities linked to the Popular Finance Group and directed the liquidators to trace money collected from the public and identify assets acquired using such funds. A Bench of Judicial Member Vinay Goel and Technical Member Ravichandran Ramasamy passed the batch of orders on October 6 on petitions moved by the Union government through the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO). The 14 entities comprise companies and limited liability partnerships belonging to the Popular Finance Group. The tribunal issued substantially similar directions in the winding-up proceedings and asked liquidators to examine the SFIO investigation report and determine where money collected from members of the public ultimately went. “ Examine the SFIO Investigation Report and other material available on record and trace the flow and end-use of funds collected from the public, ” the tribunal ruled. The liquidators have also been directed to identify properties and assets acquired from such funds and initiate appropriate proceedings for their recovery, restoration or protection for the benefit of the entities and their stakeholders. They have further been asked to invite, verify and adjudicate claims from creditors, depositors, investors and other stakeholders, besides seeking information and assistance from the SFIO, Registrar of Companies, banks, financial institutions and other investigating agencies. The directions assume significance since the SFIO investigation found that the Popular Finance Group had mobilised approximately ₹4,700 crore from members of the public. Of this, around ₹829.31 crore was attributed to the companies and LLPs covered by the investigation. According to the SFIO, the Group raised funds through fixed, recurring and savings deposits, capital contributions and debentures. It alleged that the money was routed among various group concerns and that funds collected from the public were ultimately used for purposes including the personal use of directors and designated partners. The investigation also alleged that the Group offered interest rates ranging between 9 percent and 18.18 percent to attract investors and projected its gold-loan operations as the face of its business. items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently upheld a family court order directing a man who had suffered a paralytic stroke to pay ₹10,000 per month as maintenance to his ex-wife, rejecting his defence that there were no marital relations between them and that he had married her to get a maid servant. items.title: Focus on scams of national level, not private property disputes: Madras High Court to ED
items.summary: The Madras High Court has advised the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to prioritise cases involving public money, corruption and scams of national consequence, instead of invoking the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) to probe private disputes [Ala Alagappan v The Additional Director, Directorate of Enforcement] Justice N Ramesh made the observation while granting bail to accused Ala Alagappan in a money laundering case arising out of transactions between a woman and Alagappan’s father, who was her power-of-attorney holder. “ The stringent provisions of the Act are not meant to be invoked where the dispute is, in its essence, between private individuals over private property, for which the ordinary criminal and civil law already provides," the Court said. The Court noted that the PMLA was enacted against the backdrop of international efforts to combat laundering of proceeds from serious crimes affecting the financial system and national interests. It acknowledged that cheating and criminal breach of trust are scheduled offences and that the PMLA, as presently framed, can apply to proceeds arising from every scheduled offence. However, the Court opined that the mere breadth of statutory power does not mean it should be exercised in every case falling within its reach. “ But the reach of a power is not the measure of the occasions for its use, ” the Court said. items.title: Delhi HC Justice Prateek Jalan recuses from hearing Gymkhana Club staff association's plea
items.summary: Delhi High Court Justice Prateek Jalan today recused from hearing the Delhi Gymkhana Club Staff Welfare Association’s plea challenging the Central government's move to evict the club from its Lutyens' Delhi premises. Justice Jalan recused from hearing the matter since he is a member of the club. "I would be more comfortable if somebody else hears this," he said. Justice Prateek Jalan The matter concerns proceedings initiated by the Central government to evict Delhi's Gymkhana Club from a 27.3-acre premises at Safdarjung Road in Lutyens' Delhi. The land on which the club functions was given to it on a perpetual lease in 1928. Clause 4 of the lease deed provides that the premises can be re-entered by the lessor (Central government) if required for a public purpose. In 2022, the Centre initiated proceedings before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) to take over the club's affairs, citing a violation of the terms of the lease deed and mismanagement. The NCLT allowed the prayer and ordered the appointment of 15 members to be nominated by the Centre for running the day-to-day business of the club. The NCLAT later upheld this order. On May 22 this year, the Centre passed an order terminating the club's perpetual lease. The government stated that the land, which is located near the Prime Minister’s residence and other high-security installations in Lutyens’ Delhi, was needed for “strengthening and securing of defence infrastructure,” governance facilities and other “vital public security purposes." This was challenged by members and employees of the Delhi Gymkhana Club before the Delhi High Court. On May 26, the High Court refused to pass any interim orders against the Centre's directive after Solicitor General Tushar Mehta assured that any eviction action would be taken only after due notice. Justice Avneesh Jhingan issued notice to the government in the matter in July. items.title: I came to Bengaluru to meet deleted voters: Dhruv Rathee to TNM
items.summary: “I’m not on anyone’s payroll. I’m not here for a regime change,” Dhruv Rathee told TNM in an exclusive interview. The YouTuber and influencer was in Bengaluru for the CJP-led protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls while demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. This marks a significant shift for one of India’s best-known online voices, moving from digital activism to on-the-ground mobilisation. This is the first time that Dhruv Rathee is attending a physical protest. Talking about why he felt the need to announce that he was at the protest not to bring about a regime change, he said, “As soon as I entered, coincidentally the Elon Musk news came. So people were making these conspiracy theories if my presence was connected to it or not. That’s why I wanted to clarify that I’m not on anyone’s payroll, I’m not here for a regime change. I’m just here to raise issues that concern every Indian. And every Indian should fight for these issues.” Dhruv’s reference was to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk’s accusation that “certain oligarchs” in India were obstructing the launch of its Starlink satellite broadband service in the country, even questioning if industrialist Mukesh Ambani was the “real boss” of India. About his impressions of the protest, he said, “It was crazy to see the energy of the people and how much they supported me, how much they were supporting the cause. That’s what made me enthusiastic to speak in front of them.” Talking about the CJP and their demands, he said, “I have always supported them from the beginning, even before they started the protests against the Education Minister [Dharmendra Pradhan]. I agree with their demands, first, that the Chief Election Commissioner should resign. Second, a new unbiased and neutral CEC should replace him. Thirdly, the rollback of SIR changes.” As he heads to Delhi where there is an unprecedented amount of security personnel deployed before the October 10 march called by the CJP, he said, “All I can say is that all the police personnel I’ve met are supporters of our cause. Of course some of them are compelled to do things because the order comes from above. If things really fall apart, I hope that most of them will decide to stand by the country instead of their job.” When asked about the INDIA bloc making the same demands regarding the SIR and CEC, Dhruv said, “I think it’s good that all the opposition parties are on the streets and they are united.

items.summary: The founding core of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) — founder Abhijeet Dipke, Co-Convenor Ashutosh Ranka, and spokesperson Saurav Das—has demanded the ouster of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar through resignation or impeachment, alongside a complete rollback of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. In an exclusive interview with Pooja Prasanna and Dhanya Rajendran of The News Minute, top leadership of the CJP also denounced the statutory immunity granted to the CEC and said that free and fair elections remain impossible without scrapping the SIR entirely. How can he be above the Constitution of India and rule of law? He's just an ordinary citizen. He has been given something which even the president of India or the Prime Minister of India doesn't have… It's absolutely unconstitutional," he said. Linking the issue of official immunity directly to the controversial voter roll revision, Ashutosh Ranka alleged that the legal shield was crafted specifically to protect officials executing large-scale disenfranchisement: "If the government has given him that immunity, that somewhere means they wanted to protect him because they have already decided to do something like this where they deleted 13 crore voters in a span of 2 years. There has to be an impeachment or he has to resign by himself. It is not our job to understand technicalities. There is a law which should not have been here in the first place. They have to roll back the SIR because that is the core issue,” he said. items.title: Does Gyanesh Kumar have immunity from the law? | South Central 96
items.summary: In this week's South Central, hosts Dhanya Rajendran and Anisha Sheth are joined by activist Shivasundar to discuss the nationwide protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's removal. Listen and follow on YouTube Listen and follow on Apple Listen and follow on Spotify “The wisdom of the old and the energy of youth must come together” remarks Shivasundar and adds that there are nuances that need to be cleared out, yet “morally and politically, ‘Gyanu, it is done bro,’ but legally it is a long way.” He urges civil society to introspect on why West Bengal's resistance to the SIR, largely involving Muslims, did not draw the same attention. Dhanya asks why it took so long for the anger to spread nationwide, and recalls that mass Form 7 filings were tried in Karnataka in 2023 as well. Anisha, who broke the Form 7 story in Karnataka, wonders whether vigilant civil society pushed the ECI to share more data. In the second part of the discussion, they are joined by lawyer and legal scholar Alok Prasanna, co-founder of the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy, who talks about the legal immunity enjoyed by the CEC. Alok explains that the 2023 law gives election commissioners judge-like immunity for actions beyond deciding cases, though not for conduct before their appointment. He argues the provision can be challenged and struck down, noting that the pending challenge has been complicated by a conflict-of-interest controversy involving Justice Sharma. He adds that the revised Form 6 never followed the statutory procedure, and that the wide powers the Supreme Court gave the ECI in the Bihar judgment are now being walked back. items.title: TN bye-polls: TVK wins Dharapuram and Madurantakam, boosting Vijay’s Assembly strength
items.summary: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) candidates P Sathyabama and K Maragatham Kumaravel have won the Dharapuram and Madurantakam Assembly bye-elections respectively, as per the results announced on October 9, Friday. The wins are politically significant for Chief Minister Vijay, whose TVK-led government lacks a majority of its own in the Tamil Nadu Assembly and needs the support of other parties to remain in power. The victories come after both candidates, who had won the constituencies on All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) tickets in the 2026 Assembly elections held five months ago, switched to the TVK and resigned from their seats to contest the bye-elections on their new party’s tickets. The bye-elections were held on October 6. In Madurantakam, Maragatham defeated DMK candidate Paranthamen by over 17,500 votes, while Sathyabama defeated DMK candidate Suganya by nearly 10,000 votes in Dharapuram. The TVK candidates took the lead after initial trends favoured the AIADMK, eventually finishing ahead of their DMK rivals. In the May 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, Sathyabama won the Dharapuram constituency with 81,100 votes, defeating DMK candidate T Indirani, who secured 64,373 votes, by a margin of 16,727 votes. Similarly, in Madurantakam, Maragatham Kumaravel won with 69,284 votes, defeating TVK candidate Ezhil Katharine Ezhilmalai, who secured 62,090 votes, by a margin of 7,194 votes. The results give Vijay’s party a boost as it seeks to consolidate its position in the Assembly. With the two victories, the TVK’s tally has risen to 110 seats, leaving it eight short of the 118 required for a simple majority in the 234-member Tamil Nadu Assembly. The bye-elections were held in Dharapuram, in Tiruppur district, and Madurantakam, in Chengalpattu district. Both are reserved constituencies for Scheduled Caste candidates. The contests were closely watched as an early electoral test of the TVK government and its ability to expand its support base beyond the Assembly elections. Voter turnout, however, declined in both constituencies compared with the Assembly elections held five months earlier. According to figures available on the Election Commission of India (ECI) website at 9 pm on polling day, Madurantakam recorded an approximate turnout of 86.26%, down from 93.22% in the Assembly elections. Dharapuram recorded a turnout of 80.30%, compared with 89.89% previously.
